It was the former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} of Yoshida in old {{ill|Nitta|ja|新田村 (神奈川県)|ko|닛타촌 (가나가와현)|qid=Q11503739|lt=Nitta Village}}, and is regarded as one of the strong candidate shrines for "{{ill|Sukiyamano Shrine|ja|杉山神社|qid=Q135039726}}," the only shikinaisha in Yokohama and in former {{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398}}. {{nihongo|'''Sugiyama Shrine'''|杉山神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. == Origin and history ==
There is a theory that it was worshipped by a clan that moved from {{ill|Bōsō Peninsula|ar|شبه جزيرة بوسو|az|Boso yarımadası|ceb|Bōsō-hantō|cs|Bósó|de|Bōsō-Halbinsel|es|Península de Bōsō|eu|Bōsō penintsula|fa|شبه‌جزیره بوسو|fr|Péninsule de Bōsō|id|Semenanjung Bōsō|it|Penisola di Bōsō|ja|房総半島|jv|Ujung Bōsō|ko|보소반도|nl|Boso (schiereiland)|pl|Bōsō (półwysep)|pt|Península de Bōsō|ru|Босо (полуостров)|simple|Bōsō Peninsula|th|คาบสมุทรโบโซ|tr|Bōsō Yarımadası|uk|Босо (півострів)|vi|Bán đảo Bōsō|zh|房總半島|qid=Q1022115}}<ref name="kamnavi-shinyoshida-sugiyama"/>. Its founding time is unknown. ''Musashi Shikishaki'' states, "In Tsuzuki District, at the place called Yoshida, there is a small place-name Sugiyama, and the shrine there is the true site." ''{{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qid=Q11503943}}'' (compiled in the Bunka-Bunsei period, 1804-1829) records: "Tax-exempt land 2 dan 5 se; to the north of the village; several stone steps up to a torii before the shrine; main shrine 2 ken by 2.5 ken; haiden 3 ken by 2 ken, south-facing; sacred body immovable; held by Shōfuku-ji in the village"<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyama (shinyoshida)"/> {{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō Yoshida Village}}. Sacred treasures and historical documents of this shrine had been kept by Shōfuku-ji, its former {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺|qid=Q11396755}}, but are said to have been completely lost in a fire at that temple<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama">[http://www18.ocn.ne.jp/~tugaru/sikinaisyasugiyama.html Inference on Sugiyama Shrine, the only shikinaisha of Musashi Tsuzuki District] (Tsugaru Ancient Kingdom)</ref>.

== As a shikinaisha candidate ==
The theory identifying this shrine as the shikinaisha predates the Bunka-Bunsei period when ''Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō'' was compiled. Works such as ''Historical Geography of Musashi Shikinaisha'' by late-Edo Shinto scholar Saitō Yoshihiko and local historian Hishinuma Isamu (published 1966, revised 1972 as ''Ancient Shrines of Musashi'') treat this theory as strong<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku52/ History and Culture of Kōhoku Ward: 52nd article, strong candidate for Sugiyama Shrine] (Ōkura Institute for Spiritual Culture)</ref>. Hishinuma cited the existence of a local minor place-name "Sugiyama," oral tradition in the long-established Mori family connected to this shrine claiming over 1,000 years of history, and a kofun called Asamazuka behind the Mori residence indicating a once-powerful local clan. ''History of Kōhoku Ward'' also says the Mori family name derives from "chinju-no-mori" and that the family is locally called "Sugiyama-sama"<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku53/ History and Culture of Kōhoku Ward: 53rd article, Sugiyama shrines in the ward] (Ōkura Institute for Spiritual Culture)</ref>. Nearby in Hayabuchi 3-chōme are the Kitagawa Omote-no-Ue site and {{ill|Kitagawa Shell Mound|ja|北川貝塚|qid=Q11401676}}, and local memory of a "Kaizuka-batake" aligns with the ''Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō'' note that there was a large shell mound in Tsuzuki District Yoshida village{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō Yoshida Village}}, showing ancient sites in this area have long been known<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama"/>.

Like many other candidate shrines, this shrine stands on elevated ground along the {{ill|Tsurumi River|arz|نهر تسورومى|de|Tsurumi (Fluss)|fa|تسورومیگاوا|ja|鶴見川|my|ဆွတ်ရုမိမြစ်|ru|Цуруми (река)|zh|鶴見川|qid=Q7850292}} system ({{ill|Hayabuchi River|ja|早渕川|qid=Q11511423}}).

== Other ==
No priest is stationed permanently at this shrine; it is managed concurrently by [http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=359&cd=1203043&scd=000&npg=0 Hachiman-sha] in Setogaya-chō, Hodogaya Ward.
